purpose: Resource/time series derived from the completed low-duty real-Worker lifecycle diagnostic
limits: Real Bun Workers and production client/Worker/Wasm, file-backed fetch; no browser, UI, GPU or deployment measurements
Low-duty lifecycle diagnostic; latencies are not CPU before/after performance comparisons
Per-job timings start after synchronous client submission; cycle work includes snapshots and postMessage preparation
The 1000-node force cancellation intentionally stresses the internal API beyond the UI's 300-node force limit
Routing checks mutate caller Maps and input snapshots; route value objects keep their existing immutable ownership contract
Live Worker counts track fixture owners; underlying native termination and reclamation can complete asynchronously
Rolling latency quantiles cover the latest 128 samples; heap/RSS include allocator and native Worker behavior
Heap samples alone do not establish or exclude a leak; controlled repeated GC/isolation would be needed
Each sample is one report checkpoint, approximately every 30 seconds; it is not continuous allocation or memory tracing
liveWorkers and maxLiveWorkers count logical fixture owners; native termination and resource reclamation may complete later

liveWasmCommittedBytes sums the latest actual Memory.buffer.byteLength probes for live owners, emitted before completed responses and at initialization/force probes; it is not an in-kernel peak or cumulative allocation measurement
Forced GC is Bun.gc(true) on the host VM at report checkpoints; it does not explicitly force each Worker VM to collect or the native allocator to return RSS
Host memory, JSC statistics and before/after-GC readings are sequential diagnostic samples, not an atomic snapshot
Observed ranges do not establish or exclude a memory leak and make no browser, GPU, physical-device or deployment claim
